terms.definition: A whole number greater than 1 that has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
terms.function: 7 is prime because only 1 and 7 divide it evenly.
terms.whereItIs: The amber tiles in the sieve grid.
terms.whyItMatters: Primes are the unique building blocks of all whole numbers.

terms.definition: A whole number greater than 1 that has more than two factors.
terms.function: 12 is composite because 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12 divide it.
terms.whereItIs: The struck-out tiles in the sieve grid.
terms.whyItMatters: Composite numbers can be broken into smaller factors, unlike primes.

terms.definition: A method of finding primes by repeatedly striking out the multiples of each prime found.
terms.function: Leaves only primes standing after the sift.
terms.whereItIs: The interactive sift run on the number grid.
terms.whyItMatters: It is an efficient, visual way to list all primes up to a limit.

terms.definition: Writing a number as a product of prime factors.
terms.function: 60 is written as 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 — a unique set of primes.
terms.whereItIs: The factor chain shown beneath a selected tile.
terms.whyItMatters: Every number's factorization is unique, which is why primes underpin fractions and codes.

terms.definition: A number that divides another number evenly.
terms.function: Primes have exactly two factors; composites have more.
terms.whereItIs: Counted per tile by the app's factor test.
terms.whyItMatters: Counting factors is the test that sorts primes from composites.
